messages:
jamie: FYI we just got an escalated ticket from ACME — they rotated an API key yesterday and now get a 403 when creating a service connector via the Console and API. UI shows "Forbidden: insufficient permissions (audit_id: a1b2c3)". They can still list projects but cannot create connectors. support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/12345

alex: Can you repro via curl and paste the headers/response? Also need tenant id and correlation id.

jamie: Repro from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." -X POST https://api.redwood.redwood.ai/v1/projects/123/connectors \\\n  -d '{"name":"acme-webhook","type":"webhook"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-request-id: a1b2c3
{"error":"forbidden","message":"caller lacks connector.create permission"}
```

devin: That response screams scope/role claim shrink from the IdP. Can you introspect the token or paste the id_token/access_token payload (json) so we can see scp/roles claims?

jamie: Introspection the customer ran (redacted):
```
{
  "sub": "user-789",
  "scp": "read:projects openid",
  "aud": "redwood.api",
  "exp": 1769516000
}
```

sarah: Confirmed — there's no connector write scope and no roles claim. We recently saw an Okta SCIM cleanup where a group rename caused the SCIM delta to drop the legacy group that maps to our connector-admin role. If the roles claim is missing we fall back to the scp-only check. Did the customer rename or remove a group yesterday?

jamie: Customer said they removed the legacy group "rw-connector-admins" during a naming cleanup yesterday. They didn't realize it maps to our service-connector role.

alex: Short-term workaround options:
- Admin can issue a new API key scoped with connector:create/write and deliver to the team.
- Re-add the SCIM group (or recreate mapping) so future tokens include the roles claim again.
- Support can issue an ephemeral support-scoped token (one-time) so they can finish onboarding while idp team fixes mapping.

Repro steps to verify locally:
1) Create an access token missing connector scopes/roles.
2) POST to /v1/projects/<id>/connectors -> 403.

Quick token inspect command (customer-friendly):
```
echo "eyJ..." | awk -F. '{print $2}' | base64 -d | jq .
```

devin: Extra context for eng: when delegated tokens are created we compute effective privileges = union(scp, mapped_roles). If mapped_roles is empty due to SCIM attr rename, privileges rely only on scp. Many IdPs strip group claims when group ids change, which matches this sequence.

jamie: Customer asked if our error message can be clearer (they saw generic forbidden). They want to know which scope is missing so they can fix IdP. Can we include a hint like "missing scope: write:connectors or missing role: connector-admin" in the audit?

alex: Assigning to eng-platform-identity to triage clarity of 403 + audit enrichment. Please pick up and advise whether we can safely disclose required scope in the error without leaking policy details. Need the correlation id (a1b2c3) and tenant id 123 for log lookup.

oncall-bot: created incident incident-redwood-2026-03-18-45 and paged eng-platform-identity.

alex: I will take ownership. Action items: (1) look up logs for x-request-id=a1b2c3 and tenant=123; (2) evaluate safe audit message improvement; (3) confirm if we can ship a small UI hint in Console for connector creation permission gaps.

jamie: Thanks — I'll tell the customer the short-term fixes (re-add group or request a support-scoped API key). They want urgency; I'll escalate on the ticket and share this thread. :thumbsup:

alex: Acknowledged. I'll update here once logs are attached and initial triage is done.
